name: Dryer purge valve not seating
summary: The purge valve of the desiccant dryer does not close fully after a regeneration pulse, so compressed air keeps escaping through the purge silencer. The unit replaces the loss continuously, stays loaded far longer than usual and stops reaching its cut-out pressure.

signal_moves.note: The clearest sign: the purge line carries pressure all the time instead of only during a changeover pulse.

signal_moves.note: What separates this from a loss in the plant: the line never sinks far enough to close the switch.
signal_moves.text: Low-pressure switch (D5) stays off. What separates this from a loss in the plant: the line never sinks far enough to close the switch.

signal_moves_text: Dryer purge pressure (P4) is persistently high while loaded. The clearest sign: the purge line carries pressure all the time instead of only during a changeover pulse.

checks: Listen at the purge silencer with the unit loaded; a steady hiss between changeover pulses is the fault.
Watch the purge pressure gauge through a full tower period and note whether it ever falls back.
remedy: Overhaul or replace the purge valve, then repeat the tower period test and confirm that the purge line falls back between pulses.

name: Tower changeover valve stuck
summary: The changeover valve no longer moves the drying duty from one tower to the other, so one tower is loaded forever while the other is never regenerated. The delivered air carries moisture once the working desiccant is saturated.

signal_moves.note: The tower in service never changes, which is the whole fault.
signal_moves.text: Tower in drying service (D3) stays on. The tower in service never changes, which is the whole fault.

remedy: Free or replace the changeover valve and prove a full period in both directions.

name: Leak in the distribution network
summary: Air escapes from the pipework, hoses or couplings behind the reservoirs, so the unit has to replace what the plant loses. Nothing inside the machine is faulty. The loss runs day and night, which is what separates it from a busy shift, and it grows slowly as more joints work loose.

signal_moves.note: The earliest sign, visible in the idle phase of every cycle.

checks: Close the isolation valve at the pneumatic panel with the unit stopped and watch whether the reservoir pressure still falls.
Walk the network and listen at joints, couplings and hose ends, starting with the branches changed most recently.
remedy: Seal or replace the leaking joints, hoses and couplings, then repeat the pressure-hold test with the unit stopped and the plant isolated.
